description: The seating capacity of the assigned room shall not be lower than the number of registered candidates.
The student-to-seat ratio for any examination shall not exceed a pre-defined limit.
The total number of candidates examined on a given calendar day shall not exceed an institution-specific ceiling.
The aggregate number of students present within a single building at any time shall not surpass a capacity limit set by safety regulations.
For oral examinations, the number of examinees in a time slot shall not exceed the maximum interview capacity authorised by the department.
The number of distinct examinations assigned to the same room and time slot shall not exceed a predefined maximum N .
source: Hubei University of Technology (OuYang and Chen (2010))

description: No more than N students may sit an exam at any one time.
A buffer of not less than a specified time interval shall separate consecutive examinations scheduled in the same room.
The temperature shall remain within an acceptable range, or the room must offer appropriate climate control.
The room shall remain continuously available for the entire duration of the examination.
The room must have the required equipment.
The room must have the required equipment for at least a predefined share of students taking the exam.
Preferentially assign examinations to rooms located within the candidates’ departmental building.
Certain examinations shall be scheduled exclusively in designated rooms.
Large exam halls must be scheduled in preference to smaller ones.
Exams must be scheduled to rooms near the relevant department.
Exams for the same department should be kept together.
Specific rooms may be reserved exclusively for particular degree programmes.
source: Yıldız Technical University (Güler and Geçici (2020); Güler et al. (2021))

description: A student who has consecutive exams on the same day should be assigned to the same room.
A penalty is incurred when examinations for distinct courses are placed in the same building or in adjacent rooms, so as to encourage spatial diversity.
Rooms allocated to a split examination shall, where possible, be located in the same building or campus sector.
The examination shall not be merged with any other examination.
source: Université de Technologie de Compiègne (Arbaoui et al. (2013))

description: The examination may be merged with other examinations.
Only examinations belonging to authorised categories may be merged.
Oral and written components shall not be merged into the same room.
Candidates shall be split into separate rooms according to examination end times.
Examinations of differing duration shall not be scheduled in the same room.
The number of rooms assigned to a split examination shall be minimised.
A minimum gap of ∆ hours shall separate any two examinations taken by the same student on the same day.
Subjects designated as difficult shall be placed towards the end of the examination session to mitigate early cognitive overload.
Each student’s examinations should be evenly distributed across the timetable.
source: Université Catholique de l’Ouest (Boizumault et al. (1996))

description: No student shall be required to sit more than a set number of examinations per day.
For a given academic programme, the number of examinations per day shall not exceed the programme-specific daily limit.
source: Ankara HBV University (Bayar and Uzun Bayar (2020))

description: The cumulative examination duration assigned to any student over any two consecutive days shall not exceed the maximum total duration set by policy.
Within a single academic department, the number of examinations scheduled on the same day shall not exceed the departmental daily limit.
source: Yıldız Technical University (Güler and Geçici (2020); Güler et al. (2021))

description: If a student has only one examination on a given day, that examination should be placed outside the evening time slots to reduce on-campus idle time.
The number of consecutive examinations assigned to a student within the same day shall not exceed the permitted consecutive-exam limit.
Take-away examinations should not be scheduled concurrently with in-person examinations.
A student shall not be assigned an examination in the last time slot of one day followed by another in the first slot of the next day, so as to ensure sufficient overnight rest.
The average difficulty of a student’s examinations shall be fairly distributed.
A penalty shall be applied to examinations scheduled on weekends.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: All examinations belonging to the same academic year shall be scheduled in a single designated time band (morning, afternoon, or evening).
source: University of Toronto and Carleton University (Carter et al. (1994))

description: A scheduling penalty shall be applied when a student is assigned examinations in both the period before lunch and after lunch on the same day.
Examinations for courses in the same programme and term shall not be scheduled in consecutive time slots on the same day.
A student shall not be allocated to two examinations occurring in the same time slot.
Re-sit candidates must be prevented from overlapping with another examination.
Examination clashes for each academic programme should be minimised.
source: Ankara HBV University (Bayar and Uzun Bayar (2020))

description: Examination clashes for each programme–year combination should be minimised.
source: Ankara HBV University (Bayar and Uzun Bayar (2020))

description: Scheduling should minimise clashes among elective courses.
source: Ankara HBV University (Bayar and Uzun Bayar (2020))

description: Exams A and B must not share the same period. (Equivalent to D1-4)
source: United States Military Academy in West Point (Wang et al. (2010))

description: Examinations for courses belonging to the same academic programme and term shall not share the same time slot.
Minimise the disparity in exam-slot conflicts among academic programmes and terms.
Minimise the number of students assigned to examination commissions where neither their supervisor nor referee serves as examiner.
source: Masaryk University (Kochaniková and Rudová (2013); Rudová et al. (2014))

description: Students supervised (or reviewed) by the same faculty member shall be scheduled in consecutive examination sequences so that the faculty member attends the minimum possible number of separate sequences. Equivalent to I1-10.
source: Masaryk University (Kochaniková and Rudová (2013); Rudová et al. (2014))

description: The thesis should be scheduled such that both the supervisor and the referee can attend the examination. Equivalent to I3-6.
source: Masaryk University (Kochaniková and Rudová (2013); Rudová et al. (2014))

description: The cumulative invigilation workload assigned to any staff member shall not exceed the maximum load defined by institutional policy.
source: King Saud University (Al-Negheimish et al. (2018); Hosny (2012))

description: Invigilation duties shall not be assigned in the late-evening time band more frequently than the frequency limit specified by the institution.
source: King Saud University (Al-Negheimish et al. (2018); Hosny (2012))

description: Each instructor shall have at least one unscheduled day per examination week.
source: King Saud University (Al-Negheimish et al. (2018); Hosny (2012))

description: Staff holding additional roles (e.g., administration or funded research) shall receive a reduced number of invigilation duties.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: The number of examinations invigilated by any staff member during the exam period shall not exceed the staff-duty limit specified by the institution.
source: Universiti Malaysia Pahang (Mohmad Kahar and Kendall (2014))

description: Invigilation duties shall be balanced among faculty members holding the same academic rank.
source: King Saud University (Al-Negheimish et al. (2018); Hosny (2012))

description: Chief-invigilator duties shall be evenly spread among eligible lecturers.
source: Universiti Malaysia Pahang (Mohmad Kahar and Kendall (2014))

description: Invigilation assignments shall be distributed so that each invigilator carries a comparable total duty load.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: A minimum rest period of ∆ hours shall separate consecutive invigilation duties assigned to the same staff member.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: Students supervised (or reviewed) by the same faculty member shall be scheduled in consecutive examination sequences so that the faculty member attends the minimum possible number of separate sequences. Equivalent to S3-2.
source: Masaryk University (Kochaniková and Rudová (2013); Rudová et al. (2014))

description: Minimise the number of proctor schedules containing split shifts on the same day.
Avoid evening-to-morning schedules.
Distribute evening-to-morning schedules evenly among proctors.
Allocate a greater number of invigilation shifts to proctors in higher experience classes.
Within the same experience class, assign more shifts to proctors who are available for more shifts and willing to work in more rooms.
Assign fewer unfavourable schedules to proctors in higher experience classes.
An instructor shall not invigilate an examination for which they are the principal teacher.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: Teaching staff shall not simultaneously hold the roles of teacher and invigilator for the same examination.
Where pedagogical policy requires it, the same individual may serve as teacher, subject expert, supervisor, and invigilator for a designated examination.
Of the professors assigned to a session, at least one shall be the principal examiner and at least one an external supervisor.
source: Vestfold County School Department (Avella et al. (2025))

description: There should be one instructor at each timeslot who can serve as chair.
source: Budapest University of Technology and Economics (Erdős and Kovári (2021))

description: There should be one instructor at each timeslot who can serve as secretary.
source: Budapest University of Technology and Economics (Erdős and Kovári (2021))

description: There should be at least one instructor at each timeslot who can serve as member.
source: Budapest University of Technology and Economics (Erdős and Kovári (2021))

description: An invigilator shall be available for the entire duration of the examination to which they are assigned.
A minimum buffer of ∆ hours shall separate an instructor’s own examination from any subsequent invigilation duty.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: Staff involved in project presentations or evaluations shall not be scheduled for invigilation during conflicting time blocks.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: A guard-time parameter ∆ shall be observed before an invigilator may supervise a second examination.
Instructor time-slot preferences should be honoured where feasible.
The supervisor and the referee of a thesis examination must be scheduled so that both can attend. Equivalent to S3-3.
source: Masaryk University (Kochaniková and Rudová (2013); Rudová et al. (2014))

description: Examinations for courses taught by the same instructional team shall be scheduled in different time slots.
Car-pool members always work the same shifts.
Each examination shall be supervised by at least the minimum number of invigilators specified by regulation.
Each academic department shall provide at least the departmental quota of proctoring personnel per examination day.
source: Ankara HBV University (Bayar and Uzun Bayar (2020))

description: Designated examinations shall be supervised by specifically named invigilators.
Where required, female proctors shall be assigned to examinations held for female-only cohorts. (Equivalent to E2-2)
Each campus shall supply invigilators for its own examinations using its assigned pool of teaching staff.
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: Each shift shall include any full-time proctor who is available for that shift.
A minimum of two professors qualified for the subject shall be assigned to every active examination session.
source: Vestfold County School Department (Avella et al. (2025))

description: Exam A shall be scheduled before Exam B.
source: Université Catholique de l’Ouest (Boizumault et al. (1996))

description: Exam A shall be scheduled after Exam B.
Exams A and B shall be scheduled in the same period.
source: Université de Technologie de Compiègne (Arbaoui et al. (2013))

description: Exams A and B must not share the same period. (Equivalent to S2-6)
source: United States Military Academy in West Point (Wang et al. (2010))

description: Exams sharing common questions shall be scheduled concurrently.
Exam A must precede Exam B by at least a pre-defined time interval ∆.
Exam A must follow Exam B by at least a pre-defined time interval ∆.
Exactly one exam in a designated group shall be scheduled last within that group.
Exactly one exam in a designated group shall be scheduled first within that group.
Specified pairs of exams shall be held on the same calendar day.
Exams belonging to mutually exclusive categories (e.g., two music classes) shall not be scheduled simultaneously.
Where feasible, avoid scheduling designated courses in specified examination periods.
source: United States Military Academy in West Point (Wang et al. (2010))

description: All written papers of the same subject shall be scheduled in a single period.
Exams A and B shall be scheduled in the same room at the same time.
source: University of British Columbia (Hare and Hamilton (2022))

description: An examination should be held at the same time as the regular lecture where institutional policy so requires.
source: École de technologie supérieure (Wong et al. (2002))

description: An examination must be scheduled no later than a pre-defined deadline.
An examination must be scheduled no earlier than a pre-defined release time.
An examination must be held at a fixed, pre-assigned period.
source: Université Catholique de l’Ouest (Boizumault et al. (1996))

description: The final examination for a course shall be scheduled only on weekdays that match its regular meeting pattern.
Examinations with the largest candidate counts should be scheduled early in the timetable.
High-capacity courses should be timetabled in the first week to maximise grading time for lecturers.
Finals, honours examinations, or papers subject to external moderation should appear early in the session.
Examinations with the largest candidate counts shall be scheduled towards the end of the examination session.
Designated examinations shall rotate their position within the timetable across successive academic years so that no single exam is always last.
source: University of Toronto and Carleton University (Carter et al. (1994))

description: Retain the optimised timetable from the previous year as much as possible by minimising changes.
Examinations shall be fixed in hierarchical order.
source: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals (Almaslami et al. (2023))

description: Authorised students with disabilities shall receive extra time in accordance with accessibility policy.
Students with disabilities shall be scheduled in rooms that meet accessibility standards (ramps, adapted desks, etc.).
Required assistive equipment (e.g., screen readers, enlarged-font papers) shall be available at the examination venue.
Dedicated support staff shall be assigned to assist candidates with disabilities during examinations.
Accessible examination rooms shall be reserved for invigilators with disabilities.
Students with disabilities shall be scheduled in separate rooms.
Religious convictions must be respected.
Where required, female proctors shall be assigned to examinations held for female-only cohorts. (Equivalent to I4-4)
If an examination falls on a state-specific public holiday observed by any registered candidate, the examination shall be moved to an alternative slot. (Equivalent to L1-7)
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: The scheduling algorithm shall respect the declared availability windows of students on work–study (alternance) programmes.
The availability constraints of part-time students shall be honoured when allocating examination periods.
Designated student groups may be restricted to a predefined subset of examination periods.
source: University of Toronto and Carleton University (Carter et al. (1994))

description: Foreign-exchange students shall, where feasible, be seated in separate rooms from domestic cohorts.
The assigned invigilator shall be proficient in the language of the examination.
Where practicable, examinations delivered in different languages should not occur on the same day for the same cohort of students.
Certain examination rules may apply only to specified categories of classes or students (e.g., clinical placements).
source: United States Military Academy in West Point (Wang et al. (2010))

description: Re-sit candidates should be scheduled in locations distinct from first-sit candidates.
Students enrolled in adjacent-year curricula (AJAC) shall be treated as a distinct cohort for clash-avoidance purposes.
All examinations shall be scheduled within the official examination window published by the university.
Designated examinations may be timetabled only inside a predefined subset of periods.
The length of the overall examination session shall be minimised with respect to the number of calendar days required.
source: Athens University of Economics and Business (Dimopoulou and Miliotis (2001))

description: The total number of examination days shall be minimised subject to feasibility.
Each examination period shall have a minimum duration prescribed by institutional policy.
Every examination day shall consist of a set of pre-defined time periods.
source: Athens University of Economics and Business (Dimopoulou and Miliotis (2001))

description: If an examination falls on a state-specific public holiday observed by any registered candidate, the examination shall be moved to an alternative slot. (Equivalent to E2-3)
source: MARA University of Technology (Cowling et al. (2002); Kendall and Hussin (2005))

description: Any free examination periods shall be placed at the end of the timetable.
Maximise the number of exams that could be moved to another period without disrupting the rest of the schedule.
Timetables shall allow sufficient travel time for students moving between distinct campuses or sites.
An examination shall not be split across multiple periods.
source: Université de Technologie de Compiègne (Arbaoui et al. (2013))

description: The duration of an examination assigned to a period shall not exceed the duration of that period.
source: Université de Technologie de Compiègne (Arbaoui et al. (2013))

description: A minimum transfer buffer shall separate two examinations when a candidate moves between examination centres. (Equivalent to L5-5)
Students should, where practicable, be examined on their home site.
Consecutive examinations for the same student should not be held at different sites.
Each candidate shall be assigned to a specific examination centre. (Equivalent to L5-4)
Scheduling shall account for parking capacity and expected traffic conditions around examination venues.
Each student shall be assigned to the geographically nearest examination centre, minimising travel distance.
Proctors shall not be assigned to rooms they have flagged as unacceptable or unadapted.
Usage of premium-cost resources (e.g., rented halls) shall be penalised in the objective function.
Rooms with higher rental rates shall incur a cost penalty proportional to their use.
Hiring temporary invigilation staff shall be modelled with a unit cost to be minimised.
To mitigate pandemic risks, examinations should be assigned to department-specific time slots, limiting inter-department contact.
High-capacity examinations should avoid early-morning slots to reduce congestion in public transport and lower transmission risk.
Candidates may be separated in different centres to limit pandemic risk.
Each candidate shall be assigned to a specific examination centre. (Equivalent to L3-3)
A minimum transfer buffer shall separate two examinations when a candidate moves between centres. (Equivalent to L2-4)
Every examination must be scheduled.
source: Athens University of Economics and Business (Dimopoulou and Miliotis (2001))

description: Every examination must be scheduled at least once.
source: United States Military Academy in West Point (Wang et al. (2010))

description: Every examination must be scheduled only once.
